chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from some of their companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (AS), from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

My father Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God upon them both) said to me: 'O my dear son! Take note of five (types of people) and do not befriend them, nor converse with them, nor travel with them on any road.' I said: 'O my father, who are they? Introduce them to me.'

He said: 'Beware of befriending the liar, for he is like a mirage — he draws the distant close to you, and distances what is close. Beware of befriending the immoral, for he will sell you out for a meal or less than that. Beware of befriending the miser, for he will abandon you in regard to his wealth at the time when you need him most. Beware of befriending the fool, for he intends to benefit you but harms you instead.'
And beware of befriending the one who severs family ties, for I have found him cursed in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, in three places:

God, Mighty and Majestic, says [47:22-23]: 'But if you held command, you would surely spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship. Those are the ones God has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their eyes.'

And the Mighty and Majestic says [13:25]: 'And those who break the covenant of God after its confirmation and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land — those will have the curse, and theirs will be an evil abode.'
And He says in Al-Baqara [2:27]: 'Who break the covenant of God after its confirmation and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the earth — those are the losers.'

key_terms.السَّرَاب: Mirage; the liar's distortion of reality — making the impossible seem possible and vice versa
key_terms.الْأَحْمَق: The fool/idiot; one whose poor judgment causes harm despite good intentions
key_terms.الْبَخِيل: The miser; one whose stinginess manifests especially in times of others' need
key_terms.الْفَاسِق: The immoral transgressor; one who openly violates divine law
key_terms.الْكَذَّاب: The habitual liar; one who deceives as a character trait, not a one-time mistake
key_terms.قَاطِع الرَّحِم: The severer of family ties; one who cuts off kinship relations, condemned in the Quran
key_terms.مُصَاحَبَة: Companionship, close social association; the hadith uses this term for sustained friendship or travel partnership, not mere acquaintance

ai.seo_question: What five types of people did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn warn against befriending?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS) counsels his son, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS), to avoid five harmful types of companions: the liar (who distorts reality like a mirage), the immoral person (who will betray for trivial gain), the miser (who will abandon you in your time of need), the fool (who harms while intending to help), and the one who severs family ties (cursed in three Quranic passages). The counsel was addressed within the immediate circle of the Imams, establishing a model of prophylactic social guidance rooted in Quranic authority. The severity of severing family ties (qati' al-rahim) is underlined by three explicit Quranic citations condemning those who break God's covenant — a rhetorical device that communicates the gravity of this sin above all others in the list.
